grounding.rationale: The central method and calibration procedure are directly supported by ref-012, and ref-001, ref-003, ref-005, and ref-016 support the proposed baseline or metric choices. However, the claim that manual penalties fail to generalize across domains or reward models is unsupported. Formal guarantees also need qualification: ref-012 describes an expected-cost solution for sequence-level sampling and only a heuristic for token-level decoding. References ref-014 and ref-018 inform the evaluation but are omitted from the support list.

gap.rationale: Ref-012 already identifies and addresses this exact gap using calibrated Lagrangian reward augmentation for both sequence-level and token-level inference-time alignment. The candidate specifies no clear difference from that work.

specificity.rationale: The candidate specifies dual calibration, augmented-reward BoN scoring, datasets, baselines, and measurable outcomes, drawing on ref-012, ref-014, ref-016, and ref-018. Experimental design could begin, but the safety cost, constraint threshold, calibration protocol, and N sweep remain unspecified. Llama Guard in ref-016 is a safeguard classifier, so its role as a comparable baseline needs clarification.

coherence.rationale: Dualizing an explicit safety constraint directly addresses the stated single-score limitation, and helpfulness judgments plus constraint violation rates can assess the intended tradeoff, consistent with ref-012. The weaker link is evaluation: AU-PRC measures safety prediction quality rather than the safety of selected responses, while scaling N requires specifying whether the dual variable is recalibrated.

value.rationale: Ref-012 already presents the same method, integration points, calibration strategy, and helpfulness-harmlessness evaluation. Applying it to the named benchmarks could provide replication evidence, but the candidate offers no distinct hypothesis or experimental contrast likely to change method choices beyond what ref-012 already investigates.
